issues.description: The solution repository declares the screen buffer under the symbol 'screen_buffer' (solution_repository/pixel.asm lines 4-6) but later references the symbol 'display_start' when computing addresses (solution_repository/pixel.asm lines 29 and 94). The problem statement and the template both refer to and declare the buffer as 'display_start' (problem_statement.md lines 30-33, template_repository/pixel.asm lines 20-22). This name mismatch means the solution references an undefined symbol (display_start) while declaring a differently named buffer, which will cause assembly/link errors and confuse students about the expected global symbol name.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the global buffer symbol consistent across artifacts. Either rename the declaration in solution_repository/pixel.asm from 'screen_buffer' to 'display_start' so it matches the template and problem statement, or update all references to 'display_start' in the solution to use 'screen_buffer' and update the template/problem accordingly. The simplest fix is to change the solution's .bss declaration to: 'display_start RESB 8294400'.

issues.description: The problem statement and the template consistently refer to the screen memory base as the symbol 'display_start' (problem_statement.md mentions display_start; template .bss declares display_start). The solution repository, however, declares the buffer using the name 'screen_buffer' (section .bss: screen_buffer RESB 8294400) while its code still references 'display_start' when computing addresses. This creates a naming mismatch across artifacts and an internal inconsistency inside the solution: students comparing artifacts cannot reliably map the conceptual entity 'start of the screen/display memory' to a single identifier, and the solution as provided references a label that is not declared under that name.
issues.suggested_fix: Use a single consistent identifier for the screen-memory base across all artifacts. E.g., rename the solution's declaration 'screen_buffer RESB 8294400' to 'display_start RESB 8294400' (or conversely rename the template/problem occurrences to 'screen_buffer'), and ensure all code references match that chosen name. Prefer aligning the solution to the problem/template name 'display_start' to minimize student confusion.
